<reason>The decisive fault line was B's early move to split the motion into "life extension" (cheap, fast, already conceded by A) and "new build" (where A's Vogtle/Hinkley/Flamanville critique lands hard). A never fully escaped the trap of having called life extension "genuinely cheap" in the opening, and spent the rest of the debate trying to argue that cheapness doesn't matter because the pool is "capped." But B repeatedly quantified that cap as "tens of gigawatts" across US, France, Japan, and Ontario, and argued this is large enough to matter within the 2026-2036 window while also being faster to deliver (license renewal vs. years-long interconnection queues for renewables). A never answered the queue-delay asymmetry cleanly — the claim that new reactors face "the same" queues doesn't address that already-operating reactors have already cleared theirs, which was B's sharper point in the Pressure Questions round (Q2) and B4.1. A's Q1 in Pressure Questions was strong (forcing PRO to rely on new-build track record for scale), but B's answer (A4.1, fleet framing) at least offered a coherent rebuttal, treating life-extension as sufficiently large-scale to satisfy the motion's demand, which A never fully dismantled — A only reasserted "capped" without quantitatively engaging the "tens of gigawatts" figure. Meanwhile, B's own pressure question (never priced a per-ton nuclear-new-build cost) went unanswered by A across multiple rounds — A repeatedly asserted renewables are "cheaper per ton" without ever supplying the comparative figure B demanded, which B highlighted effectively in both rebuttal 2 and closing. Both sides had legitimate points and B's UAE/Korea comparators were fairly incapacitated by A's "authoritarian-adjacent, not comparable" rebuttal, but B recovered by pivoting hard to life-extension as the core mechanism, which A's own opening concession made hard to fully deny. On balance B's argument architecture was more internally consistent and better defended against direct pressure, while A relied more on assertion of comparative renewable cost-per-ton without ever substantiating it, despite being asked twice.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B's Pressure Questions Q1/Q2 (B3.1-B3.2) demanding a priced per-ton renewable cost and highlighting that "already connected" reactors don't face the queue delays renewables do — a demand A never satisfied in Rebuttal 2 or Closing, leaving that specific pressure point live and unresolved in B's favor.</best_rebuttal>
